encoding_variations: Benefit amount + frequency: the same monthly figure may be printed as '$2,540/mo' or as an annual '$30,480/yr' — payment_frequency is the disambiguator that fixes the annualization
Continuance is stated as 'payable for life,' 'lifetime,' '10-year certain,' or with a benefit_end_date — capture both lifetime_or_term_certain and benefit_end_date
Gross vs net: award letters often state gross with a separate withholding line; keep both figures

open_questions.q: net vs gross for income — underwriting typically qualifies on gross (often grossed-up for non-taxable retirement income).
open_questions.recommendation: keep both; the gross-up is a downstream calculation

open_questions.q: survivor_benefit_terms as free text — it is prose.
open_questions.recommendation: free str now; if a continuance rule later needs a structured survivor flag, add a boolean then

notes: No rules read this document today (rule_count 0); there is no rule floor. An award letter establishes the amount, frequency, and continuance of retirement income. Fields earn a place by identity, PII protection, disambiguation, or processor use.

plan_or_claim_number_masked needs _PII_FIELDS registration, pre_masked true (catalog sensitivity restricted; the field is already the masked form). Retiree/beneficiary name is standard sensitivity → identity field, not registry PII.
Prompt hint (doc-level): Do NOT annualize or judge continuance — extract gross, frequency, commencement, and lifetime/term verbatim; a rule/tag computes qualifying income.
